test_title: PYST 6: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Ilbert Bill controversy of 1883 was related to which issue?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rights of Indian judges**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Ilbert Bill** was a legislative measure introduced in **1883** during the viceroyalty of **Lord Ripon**. It was drafted by **Sir Courtenay Peregrine Ilbert**, who was the **Legal Member** of the **Viceroy's Executive Council**.

• The primary objective of the bill was to address the issue of **judicial disqualification** based on race. Before this bill, according to the **Criminal Procedure Code of 1873**, **Indian judges** and **magistrates** in the interior (mofussil) were not allowed to try **European British subjects** in criminal cases, even if the Indian judge was senior in rank.

• The bill proposed to grant **Indian District Magistrates** and **Sessions Judges** the same jurisdiction and **Rights of Indian judges** as their European counterparts to try Europeans. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*

• The bill did not deal with the **Introduction of income tax**. Income tax in **India** was first introduced in **1860** by **James Wilson** to overcome the financial difficulties caused by the **Revolt of 1857**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*

• The **Expansion of railways** was a process that began much earlier, with the first train running between **Bombay** and **Thane** in **1853** under **Lord Dalhousie**. The **Ilbert Bill** had no relation to railway infrastructure. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

• The **Indianisation of the army** was a political demand that gained significant momentum during the **20th century**, particularly after **World War I**, and was not the subject of the **1883** controversy. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Lord Ripon**, who served as **Viceroy** from **1880** to **1884**, is regarded as one of the most liberal administrators in **British India**. He is known for the **Repeal of the Vernacular Press Act (1882)** and the **Resolution on Local Self-Government (1882)**.

• The **European community** in **India**, especially the **indigo and tea planters** in **Bengal**, reacted with extreme hostility to the bill. They viewed it as an insult to their racial superiority and formed the **European and Anglo-Indian Defence Association** to protest against it.

• This organized resistance by the British settlers is often referred to as the **White Mutiny**. They raised a fund of over **1.5 lakh rupees** and lobbied the government in **London** to withdraw the bill.

• Due to the intense pressure, a **compromise** was reached in **January 1884**. The amended bill allowed **Indian judges** to try Europeans, but the accused were given the right to demand a **jury**, of which at least **50%** of the members had to be **Europeans or Americans**.

• The **Ilbert Bill controversy** acted as a major catalyst for **Indian Nationalism**. It demonstrated to the **Indian intelligentsia** that they would never receive equal treatment under **British rule** without a unified political struggle.

**Important Points__**

• The controversy highlighted the **institutionalized racism** inherent in the **British colonial administration**. Even liberal reforms were thwarted by the collective pressure of the ruling race.

• **Surendranath Banerjee** and the **Indian National Association** (founded in **1876**) played a pivotal role in organizing counter-protests and support for the bill, which helped in the **political awakening** of the Indian middle class.

• The lessons learned from the **Ilbert Bill** agitation directly contributed to the formation of the **Indian National Congress** in **December 1885** at **Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College** in **Bombay**.

• The **compromise of 1884** was seen as a defeat for **Lord Ripon**, who eventually resigned from his post and returned to **England**, though he remained a hero to the **Indian people** for his efforts toward equality.
